name: Sinding-Larsen-Johansson Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Sinding-Larsen-Johansson Disease

criteria.description: Localized pain at the inferior pole of the patella exacerbated by activity
Palpable tenderness over the inferior patellar pole
Radiographic evidence of fragmentation or irregularity of the inferior patellar apophysis
Symptoms worsen with jumping, running, or kneeling activities
No signs of infection or acute trauma to the knee

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of localized anterior knee pain and tenderness at the inferior patellar pole with radiographic evidence of apophyseal irregularity
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; MRI may be used if diagnosis is uncertain.

imaging: Radiographs showing fragmentation or irregularity of the inferior patellar apophysis
MRI demonstrating edema and inflammation at the patellar tendon insertion
Ultrasound revealing thickening and hypoechogenicity of the patellar tendon insertion
other: Clinical examination revealing localized tenderness and pain on resisted knee extension

distinguishingFeatures: Pain and swelling localized to the tibial tuberosity rather than the patella
Radiographic changes at the tibial tubercle apophysis
Pain more diffuse along the patellar tendon
Absence of apophyseal fragmentation on imaging
Diffuse anterior knee pain without localized tenderness at the inferior patellar pole

redFlags: Severe worsening pain unresponsive to conservative treatment
Signs of infection such as fever, redness, or warmth over the knee
Acute traumatic injury with inability to extend the knee
references: Kujala UM, Kvist M, Heinonen O. Sinding-Larsen-Johansson syndrome: a follow-up study. J Pediatr Orthop. 1985;5(1):76-79.
Micheli LJ, Fehlandt AF. Overuse injuries to tendons and apophyses in children and adolescents. Clin Sports Med. 1992;11(4):713-726.
